elements.element: Vendor defends Customer (and affiliates) against covered third-party claims
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim"

elements.element: Coverage: third-party claims alleging services or deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: "(a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Coverage: data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: "(c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor"
"(d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"
"shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim"
"allow the indemnifying party to control the defence with counsel of its choice"
"provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense"

elements.element: Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: "arising out of content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services ... or Customer's breach of Applicable Law"
"an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"
"Customer's unauthorized modification ... combination with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor ... Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer"
"procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them ... Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees"

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No super-cap appears; 21.3 merely lists "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims with no 3× annual fees cap.

offending_extra_words: The indemnifying party shall not settle a claim in a way that imposes liability, an admission, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party without its prior written consent.
The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its own cost.
procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them with functionally equivalent, non-infringing items
Vendor's obligation in Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification
reasons: Preferred level is complete: Vendor defence/indemnity for Customer and Affiliates covering IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation procedure and a Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
Fallback is not satisfied because the required 3× annual fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity is absent, but that is irrelevant to the locked preferred target.

Minimality fails: the insertion imports fallback-only material (exclusions in 20.2 and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in 20.5) and adds language outside the preferred prose — hold-harmless wording, a Customer defence duty, participation rights and settlement-consent mechanics beyond notice, control and cooperation.
Intent is preserved: the clause fills an absent article, cures the dangling cross-references in 9.3 (Section 20.5) and 21.3, and uses only defined terms without contradiction.

Drafting note: the new numbered heading was anchored after an existing section heading rather than after the preceding section's final body paragraph, which risks misplacement of the inserted article.
